style: Afrofuturist Atlantis: a Black harbour city that kept its flood. Old walls carry a salt line at four metres. Ruins are mended in white ceramic seamed with light. Rusted teal steel, painted plywood, wet asphalt as a mirror. Photographic, 35mm, practical light sources, humid air. The future here is repaired and inherited, never chrome or sterile. Everyone in the city is Black, of every age; elders are present and honoured.
skin: Deep brown skin lit with full tonal range: a warm key, a rim light in the district's glow colour. Never crushed to a flat silhouette unless the beat asks for one.

POET.lock: THE POET: a Black man in his thirties, the one who speaks. Close-cropped hair, short beard. Always in matte black: fitted mock-neck long sleeve, black trousers, black boots. A thin seam of white light runs from his collar to over his heart, like mended ceramic; it brightens when he speaks. Unhurried, hands open.
holds: seam of light over the heart

EX.lock: THE EX: a Black man of the same age, the man he loved and is leaving. Leaner and taller. Locs gathered at the nape. A long sodium-orange coat with a teal lining. A vape whose ember pulses cyan-white in his hand. Seen from behind or in profile; he turns his face to camera only when a beat says so.

cast.PAIR: The two men were lovers. Their intimacy is shown by distance closing or opening, by hands, by foreheads, by who turns away. Tender and adult, never a spectacle, never a joke.
